mentl/349c334:
march CLEAN, m2 == m3, census 0, 34.94s / 2323940 KB (under ceiling).

THE SENTENCE THAT WAS AN ALIBI. PLAN §5.O read "whole program actions keep
their honest bounds: compile is O(reachable image) ... the law bans accidental
super-constant lookup; it does not ban the structural walks whose output is the
requested value." That was not an accounting. It licensed re-deriving, on every
run, a result that could not have changed — and it was written by the same hand
that wrote the code doing it.

MEASURED, WHICH IS WHY IT IS GONE. The compiler persists its analyzed image and
restores it, then re-runs saturate, lower, reachability, the gate and emit over
the restored graph every single run. A five-line two-module program compiles
warm in 5.75s against a ~2.0s process floor and delivers 78KB — ~20KB/s, so the
3.8s is DERIVATION, not delivery. And the driver printed "warm: image current —
nothing re-derived" through all of it: true of INFERENCE, false of the compile.
A scoped claim rendered as an absolute, one layer under the paragraph that
excused it.

THE LAW SEPARATES THE TWO COSTS THE OLD SENTENCE CONFLATED:
  DERIVATION — computing a fact. O(1) amortized, no exceptions. If the inputs
  did not change the cost is ZERO. Carried-Truth extended over TIME: re-deriving
  across runs is the same violation as re-deriving across call sites.
  DELIVERY — handing over a value. O(what was asked for). You cannot produce N
  bytes in fewer than N operations; that is information, not overhead.
So the whole law: THE COST OF AN OPERATION IS THE SIZE OF THE ANSWER IT WAS
ASKED FOR, AND NOTHING ELSE. Falsifiable and gate-shaped — change nothing,
compile again, measure.

mentl/34f829e:
NEW: std/runtime/memory.ka

Memory and Alloc were used 131+ times across the codebase but
declared NOWHERE. The emitter recognized operation names by
string magic. The developer had to 'just know' that store_i32,
load_i32, store_i8, load_i8, mem_copy, i32_xor, and alloc
existed as performable operations.

Now declared as proper effects with full signatures, param
comments, and resume discipline annotations:

  effect Memory {
    store_i32(Int, Int) -> ()       // (addr, value)
    load_i32(Int) -> Int            // (addr) -> value
    store_i8(Int, Int) -> ()        // (addr, byte)
    load_i8(Int) -> Int             // (addr) -> byte
    mem_copy(Int, Int, Int) -> ()   // (dst, src, n)
    i32_xor(Int, Int) -> Int        // (a, b) -> a XOR b
  }

  effect Alloc {
    alloc(Int) -> Int               // (size) -> ptr
  }

Pure documented as the empty effect row (EfClosed([])), not an
effect with operations.

Alloc separated from Memory because with Memory + !Alloc is
load-bearing for real-time audio paths where allocation is
forbidden. The effect row makes this constraint checkable.

Every effect in Inka now has a source declaration:
  Memory     -> std/runtime/memory.ka
  Alloc      -> std/runtime/memory.ka
  Pack       -> std/runtime/binary.ka
  Unpack     -> std/runtime/binary.ka
  Filesystem -> std/compiler/types.ka
  (all compiler effects -> std/compiler/types.ka)

sonido/34c352b:
Three correctness bugs and one RT-safety violation fixed:

- Bypass now outputs dry signal via wet_dry_mix crossfade instead of
  fading to silence. Three-phase borrow-safe pattern: save dry input to
  per-node bypass_buf, process effect (keeps state warm), then crossfade.
- Schedule swap runs only the new schedule and blends from cached
  previous-block output, eliminating double-processing of effects and
  stale-index hazards from topology changes.
- Latency compensation delay lines persist across blocks as fields on
  ProcessingGraph instead of being reconstructed (zeroed) every callback.
- BufferPool moved from per-block allocation to persistent field, sized
  at compile() and reused — zero heap allocations in run_schedule().

Additional cleanup:
- SplitCopy uses fixed [usize; 8] array instead of Vec (no_std friendly)
- GraphEngine uses persistent scratch buffers instead of per-call Vecs
- Removed dead code: BypassState struct, Edge.buffer_idx, prev_nodes_snapshot
- CompiledSchedule stores buffer_count/delay_sample_counts (metadata)
  instead of owning BufferPool/CompensationDelay (runtime objects)

noodles/34fbcd4:
npm run probe:music rolls thousands of songs through model.js and
measures the notes; over 4000 rolls it found the dice dealing wrong
ones in specific, fixable ways.

- Degrees are not functions. Major-key degree decks were dealt into
  every mode (I-V-vi-IV in lydian is I-V-vi-#iv°): 26% of songs held a
  diminished triad, 71% of phrygian ones, 6.6% opened on one. Each mode
  now deals its own idiomatic moves from its major and minor triads;
  statics lean home; wander keeps its surprise without the dim chord.
  0% of songs now, 70% open on the tonic (was 50%). Narrows D23.
- The pad stacked every extension above the triad (spans to 23
  semitones, top-line leaps of a fourth+ on 18% of changes). chordVoicing
  moves into the model and sounds the triad, the seventh and one color
  tone, avoid notes dropped, placed rub-free by a small search. Top-line
  leaps 5%, sevenths kept 100%; the staff engraves the same voicing.
- Bass roots land in A1-G#2 (half of all rolls sat in octave 1, which a
  phone can't make); the melody sits over the pad (it was under the
  pad's top voice on 47% of notes); the random pad octave is gone.
- Melody notes that rub the voiced pad (a minor 2nd or 9th) move to the
  nearest clean tone unless they are passing tones: 7.9% -> 1.7% of
  melody time, leaps and range unchanged.
- The polymeter bass pedals the real tonic (it pedaled the scale note
  just above C, the leading tone in D major); the vamp outro skips
  mixolydian's diminished iii; a roll features at most one color insert
  (each track drew one 2 times in 3); the arp climbs in pitch order.

Gates: smoke, vamp probe, calibrate master spread 1.9 dB.

stoop/3401b31:
Four friends tried to start a punk zine on this and hit four walls, none of
which any existing suite would have found: every other suite drives the app
the way somebody who already knows it works would.

Two name boxes become a roster. Entries were already stored against an id
rather than a spelling, but only two ids existed and migrate() collapsed
anything else onto the first of them, so a piece arriving from a third
person's copy lost its byline on the way in. The roster takes as many people
as write for you, ids for anyone after the founding pair are random so two
scenes cannot hand out the same one, an incoming roster is merged rather than
overwritten, and a byline with nobody attached seats a placeholder instead of
being filed under somebody else's name. A machine with nothing of its own
adopts the roster the file brought, which is the case that was silently
refusing names: defaulting first took the ids a and b, and the real names
arriving in the file were skipped as already present.

Ringing the bell archives the issue and starts the next one, so the sheet on
screen was never the issue that had just gone to the shelf. Publishing then
printing — which is the obvious order — produced fifty blank copies. The
press now says which issue the draft is and where the published one went, a
new draft starts with its section headings and no body text so an unwritten
sheet reads as unwritten, and anything that spends paper, ink or a file asks
before committing a blank one.

The sample notebook was load-bearing: its pieces rode into the first real
issue and the only way out was a reset that put them back. START EMPTY clears
everything and leaves the press blank.

The cover said STOOP ZINE until you discovered the heading was editable, and
that name reached the flyer and the exported filename. It is a field in
settings now.

FORMAT.md gains the roster, since an issue file carries it and a reader has to
know not to overwrite its own or drop a byline it does not recognise.
